query: What signals suggest a travel expense will be declined?

per_column.name: travel_related_expense_mention
per_column.rationale: Whether the description mentions travel is an antecedent attribute of the expense, knowable at submission time, and plausibly related to approval/decline of travel expenses. Legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: The category/type of asset being expensed is an ex-ante attribute that can plausibly influence decline rates (e.g., vehicles vs software). Lies outside the focus.

per_column.name: department_requestor
per_column.rationale: The requesting department is a pre-outcome attribute with plausible predictive signal on decline likelihood; largely restates the existing department column but is still a valid predictor variable.

per_column.name: asset_type_specificity
per_column.rationale: How specifically the item is described (specific model vs generic category) is derivable from the request text before the decision and could correlate with scrutiny/decline. Legitimate, if weak.

per_column.name: expense_automation_signal
per_column.rationale: Whether the expense was manually entered vs auto-logged is a submission-time attribute that can plausibly relate to review outcome. Outside the focus, carries potential signal.

per_column.name: processing_delay_indicator
per_column.rationale: Processing delay is measured across/after the handling of the expense and depends on the processed_date relative to opening; the delay is realized during/after the decision, so it is only knowable at or after the outcome. This leaks the resolution process rather than predicting it ex ante.

per_column.name: expense_source_tracking_presence
per_column.rationale: Presence of a source/tracking id is an attribute of the record available at submission; plausibly correlated with completeness and thus decline. Weak but legitimate predictor.

judge.rationale: Most added columns are ex-ante attributes of the expense (travel mention, asset category, department, description specificity, automation source, source-tracking presence) that lie outside the focus and could plausibly carry signal about decline, so they qualify as legitimate predictors. However, several are largely re-derivations of existing columns (department, asset/source id presence) offering limited incremental leverage, and most are weak or generic categorical flags rather than strongly discriminating features. One column (processing_delay_indicator) reflects the handling timeline realized at/after the decision and risks leakage. As a set the incremental predictive value beyond the original table is modest.
